title: The approval that approved itself
blurb: The requester named their own approvers and states advanced twice.
prompt: A spend request was approved by the requester's own account because the draft accepted caller-named approvers, and one approver's double-click advanced two steps of the chain. Review it, fix it, and prove approvers come from policy and one decision moves one step.
aiNote: The draft resolves approvers from the request body instead of the pinned policy, so a requester can name a friendly or themselves, and its advance logic accepts any approval item from a list, so a duplicated decision skips a step entirely.
testIdea: Submit with caller-named approvers and assert policy resolution overrides them; double-decide as one approver and assert the chain advances one step; time out eligibility and assert the decision is denied.
followUps: When is delegation legitimate versus a bypass?
